_doc: The field, as a committed manifest. Every tool we benchmark AND every tool we
deliberately do not — with the reason, so 'why isn't X here' is answered in the
repo instead of in someone's head.
gatherable=true means the tool has a local CLI that builds a persistent index we
can wall-clock on a fresh tree. gatherable=false tools are real competitors that
cannot share a row honestly (SaaS, cloud-indexed, no persistent graph, or a
fundamentally different artifact); they are listed so the field is complete.
ref: pinned commit. Fetched shallow (git fetch --depth 1 origin <sha>), so the
clone stays small AND the version is exact. setup.py records whether the pin
took or it fell back to the default branch — a floating version must never be
reported as a pinned one.
SESSION FIELDS (added 2026-08-15 for benchmarks/session/session.py, the
multi-pass runner). The one-pass runner measures a cold build; the session
runner measures build -> query -> edit -> re-index -> query, which is what an
agent actually costs. Both read THIS manifest — one field, one source of
truth.
incremental      argv/list-of-argv run after an edit. Absent means the tool
has no incremental path and the session runner will re-run
`build`, reporting it as a full rebuild rather than
quietly calling it 'warm' (the 2026-07-24 GitNexus bug in
AUDIT.md).
session_build    argv/list, when the session runner needs a different shape
than the one-pass `gather` string (which is prose, not argv).
session_query    argv template; {corpus} {index} {query} expand.
query_by_class   per-question-class override (locate/relate/staleness).
query_field      which question field feeds the command; search tools take
`q_literal` (the exact symbol) — deliberately their best case.
answers_classes  classes the tool can answer AT ALL. A class not listed is
reported n/a and EXCLUDED from that score. Scoring a line
matcher 0/10 on 'who calls this' is a rigged test, not a
finding.
EXTERNAL YARDSTICK: benchmarks/locbench/ scores ctx-optimize on Loc-Bench
(czlll/Loc-Bench_V1, LocAgent ACL 2025) — somebody else's ground truth and
baselines. We enter its RETRIEVAL tier (no LLM), whose published peers are
BM25 38.69% / CodeRankEmbed 52.55% file Acc@5; LocAgent's 84.59% is the
agentic tier and is NOT our comparison. Competitors here could take the same
ranked-list protocol — that is the next step toward an external comparison.
BOUNDARY CLASSES (added 2026-08-15, ADR 13). Every scored question used to be
code-locate, so the boundary lane / routes / doc links had no regression net:
a rule could stop matching and no number would move. These classes exist to
make that visible, NOT to raise our score — we are alone in several of them,
which makes a comparative number meaningless there. Per-class always, never
blended; a tool that does not claim a class is n/a, never 0; breadth is the
capability matrix, not an average.
boundary/egress   what external services does this call
boundary/config   which env vars does it read / which are credentials
boundary/process  what command-line tools does it run
api-surface       what endpoints does it expose
transport-shape   how does it reach a peer (transport in the ANSWER)
doc-to-code       where is this documented — scores 0 today, see below
query_as: lets one CLASS use more than one command (both config questions are
boundary/config, but the credentials one needs the sensitive filter). What is
measured stays separate from how a tool answers it.
KNOWN ZERO, DELIBERATELY NOT HIDDEN: doc-to-code scores 0/1. ADR 10 (doc
citations) is DRAFT and section->code edges measure ZERO in the store, so the
capability does not exist yet. It is pointed at `query` rather than marked
n/a because n/a would read as 'not our category' when the truth is 'not built
yet'. It should go 0 -> 1 when ADR 10 lands; if it does not, that is a bug.
ALSO KNOWN: `query` cannot reach boundary facts at all (ADR 14 — querying
api.openai.com does not return the node whose id IS api.openai.com). So the
boundary classes are answered by `nodes --kind port --where ...`, the verb
that works today. The natural-language path scoring ~0 is recorded in the
session results as natural_query_gap rather than quietly routed around.

tools.name: ctx-optimize
tools.note: baseline. Wiki off by default since v0.12, so this column is NOT comparable to the 2026-07-24 run, which included wiki generation in the gather.

tools.name: graphify
tools.note: PyPI package is 'graphifyy', binary is 'graphify'. The repo appears to have moved from safishamsi/ to Graphify-Labs/ since the 2026-07-24 run; setup tries the pinned URL first, then repo_alt, and records which resolved. Queries hard-cap at 512MB of graph.json (GRAPHIFY_MAX_GRAPH_BYTES) — on linux it builds a 1.2GB graph it then refuses to read, so the suite sets the cap explicitly and records that it did.

tools.name: codegraph
tools.note: local node-sqlite. Telemetry disabled so no network call lands in a timed path. `init` refuses on an initialized dir; `sync` is its own designated incremental path, so that is the warm row.

tools.name: gitnexus
tools.note: monorepo; gitnexus-shared must build before gitnexus. --index-only excludes embeddings/skills/PDG, i.e. its fastest honest path. Build command corrected 2026-08-15: the pinned tree has NO npm workspaces — the package lives in the gitnexus/ subdirectory. The previous  command matched a different layout, which means the dist/ present in the arena before this fix was NOT built from the pinned SHA.

tools.name: codegraphcontext
tools.note: added 2026-08-05, not in the 2026-07-24 run. ref null = default branch; setup records the resolved SHA so the run is still reproducible after the fact. May require a graph backend — if it does, it drops to gatherable=false with the reason recorded rather than being quietly skipped.

tools.name: ast-grep
tools.gatherable_reason: no index — it scans the tree on every query, so it has no cold-gather row to occupy
tools.note: joins the QUERY axis only, as the scan-every-time control against a pre-built index.

tools.name: repomix
tools.gatherable_reason: packs a repo into one LLM-ready file rather than building a queryable graph — no query verb to time
tools.note: 26.2k stars, ~255k npm downloads/mo. Different artifact; comparing pack time to gather time would be a category error. Listed because it is a real alternative users choose instead of a graph.

tools.name: serena
tools.gatherable_reason: LSP-over-MCP with no persistent graph — nothing to build, nothing to size
tools.note: 25.2k stars, 40+ languages. Would need a separate latency-only methodology.

tools.name: claude-context
tools.gatherable_reason: embeddings-based; requires an embedding provider, so it cannot share a no-LLM/no-network row

tools.name: augment / cody / greptile / deepwiki
tools.gatherable_reason: SaaS or cloud-indexed — no single-machine deterministic path, and code egress makes them a different product category

tools.name: gnu-global (gtags)
tools.why_not: ADJACENT CATEGORY, not a competitor (owner call 2026-08-15). Classic C symbol indexer for a HUMAN in an editor doing jump-to-definition: no agent interface, no structured output, no cross-language graph, no docs/config/deps in one artifact, no 'what breaks if I change X'. Nobody evaluating ctx-optimize is choosing between it and gtags. Listed so the field is complete and so 'why isn't gtags here' is answered in the repo. Its ~37M lines/min build speed is real and is why our speed claim must NAME its cohort (agent graph tools) rather than say 'the next tool'.

tools.name: zoekt
tools.why_not: ADJACENT CATEGORY, not a competitor (owner call 2026-08-15). Trigram TEXT search — a search box, not a symbol graph. Cannot answer 'who calls this' and does not claim to. Same role as ripgrep in this field: a speed reference from a different category, listed for completeness.

tools.name: scip indexers (scip-go, scip-typescript, ...)
tools.why_not: ADJACENT CATEGORY, not a competitor in the agent-context market (owner call 2026-08-15), though the closest in KIND: compiler-precise edges, strictly more accurate than our heuristic tiers, at the cost of a working build per language. Relevant to docs/CRITIQUE.md #8 (we have a cost/coverage argument against SCIP, never an accuracy one), not to the benchmark cohort.

tools.name: ripgrep
tools.why_not: ADJACENT CATEGORY, not a competitor — an on-the-fly regex matcher with no index and no symbol graph. Included in the SESSION runner as the honest floor: it is indexless (build and incremental are a true 0s) and can never be stale, which are real advantages a build-time-only benchmark hides. It is excluded from `relate` because no line matcher can answer 'what breaks if I change this'.
